NDT training in Hawaii: how it works for Hawaii employers and technicians

Short answer: Atlantis NDT delivers ASNT SNT-TC-1A NDT training for Hawaii employers and technicians at Level I, II and III in UT, PAUT, TOFD, RT, MT, PT, VT and ET. Theory runs live online (Hawaii time-zone sessions can be arranged) and practical training runs onsite at your facility on Oahu or the neighbour islands under ASNT Level III oversight. Your employer certifies you against its written practice. Atlantis has no training centre in Hawaii. Quotes are on request.

Hawaii is one of the hardest places in the United States to train NDT technicians. The islands are thousands of miles from the mainland training schools, flights and hotels for a multi-week course add up quickly, and pulling a technician off a small team for weeks can stall a whole inspection programme. At the same time, Hawaii's environment is brutal on steel: salt air, humidity and year-round warmth drive corrosion on everything from piping and tanks to bridges, piers and power plant structures.

That combination is why the delivery model matters more here than the course catalogue. The most practical route for most Hawaii employers is to complete theory live online, then bring practical training and examinations onsite so the crew never leaves the island. Atlantis trains to ASNT SNT-TC-1A. Request a Hawaii training quote.

ASNT Level I, II and III courses available in Hawaii

All courses are available as live online theory plus onsite practical, with Level III-reviewed content aligned to SNT-TC-1A. The table shows how each method maps to Hawaii work.

MethodLevelsWhat Hawaii employers use it forPrerequisite
Ultrasonic Testing (UT)I, II, III prepCorrosion thickness surveys on piping, tanks and marine structures; weld inspection on repairs and new fabricationNone for Level I; Level I plus documented experience for Level II
Phased Array UT (PAUT)II, III prepCorrosion mapping on refinery and power piping; encoded weld inspectionUT Level II recommended
Time-of-Flight Diffraction (TOFD)II, III prepThick-section weld sizing on vessels and heavy pipingUT Level II recommended
Radiographic Testing (RT)I, II, III prepWeld radiography on piping and fabrication; profile RT for corrosion under insulationNRC and Hawaii Department of Health requirements for sources and X-ray (see below)
Magnetic Particle Testing (MT)I, II, III prepCracks in welds, structural steel, cranes and lifting gear; marine and pier structuresNone for Level I
Liquid Penetrant Testing (PT)I, II, III prepStainless and non-ferrous components, aircraft parts, valves and pumpsNone for Level I
Visual Testing (VT)I, II, III prepCorrosion and coating condition, weld visual, bridge and structure inspectionNone for Level I
Eddy Current Testing (ET)I, II, III prepAircraft structure and wheel inspection in MRO; heat-exchanger and condenser tubes at power plantsNone for Level I

Because Hawaii teams are small, multi-method technicians are especially valuable. A common path is VT and UT thickness first, then MT and PT, then weld UT or RT, with PAUT corrosion mapping and ET tubing as advanced skills. Senior technicians can prepare for the ASNT Level III examinations via ASNT Level III training; a Level III on staff is particularly valuable in Hawaii, where flying one in for every examination is slow.

SNT-TC-1A certification path in Hawaii, step by step

  1. Employer written practice. Training and experience hours, examinations, vision testing, the responsible Level III, recertification and records. See written practice development.
  2. Classroom training hours by method and level. Recommended minimums: training requirements matrix. In Hawaii this is the part that moves online most easily.
  3. On-the-job experience, documented and supervised, on the employer's real work.
  4. General examination on method theory.
  5. Specific examination on the employer's procedures, equipment, codes and acceptance criteria.
  6. Practical examination on real specimens, administered and graded under a Level III, onsite in Hawaii.
  7. Vision examination for near vision and colour contrast at the written practice's interval.
  8. Employer certification once the file is complete.
  9. Recertification at the specified interval. Planning recertification examinations to coincide with an onsite training visit saves a second trip.

Full framework: SNT-TC-1A training and certification.

Online, live-virtual or onsite NDT training for Hawaii crews

Atlantis has no training centre in Honolulu or anywhere in Hawaii. For island employers, that is less of a limitation than it sounds, because the realistic alternative is flying people to the mainland.

  • Live online theory with sessions scheduled to work in Hawaii–Aleutian Standard Time, which is several hours behind the mainland. See NDT training online.
  • Onsite practical at your facility on Oahu or a neighbour island, using your instruments and specimens representative of your work, such as corroded pipe, tank plate or weld samples.
  • Combined visits. Practical training, examinations, recertifications and written practice review planned into a single onsite visit to minimise travel.
  • Corporate programmes: see corporate NDT training.

Scheduling is planned around refinery and power plant outages, shipyard availability and your crew's workload. Ask about onsite training for your Hawaii crew; cohort and onsite quotes are normally returned within one business day.

Where NDT technicians work in Hawaii

  • Naval ship repair. Pearl Harbor Naval Shipyard and Intermediate Maintenance Facility maintains submarines and surface ships, with weld and structural inspection under NAVSEA requirements and its own qualification programme. Many roles require US citizenship and a clearance.
  • Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam and other installations. Military facilities across Oahu, including Army installations and Marine Corps Base Hawaii, generate structural, fuel system, tank and piping inspection, often through contractors.
  • Refining and fuels. Par Hawaii's Kapolei refinery and Hawaii's fuel terminals and pipelines need corrosion surveys, weld inspection and tank inspection to API 510, 570 and 653 programmes and ASME codes.
  • Power generation. Oil-fired and other generating plants operated by Hawaiian Electric and independent producers across the islands require boiler tube, condenser, piping and structural inspection during outages.
  • Aviation MRO. Commercial airline maintenance at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport and inter-island operations rely on ET, PT, UT and VT to OEM manuals and FAA-approved maintenance programmes.
  • Harbours and marine structures. Honolulu Harbor, Kalaeloa Barbers Point Harbor and neighbour-island ports have piers, sheet piling, cranes and fuel lines that corrode fast in the marine environment.
  • Bridges and transit. The Hawaii Department of Transportation's bridges and the Honolulu elevated rail system involve steel and weld inspection to AWS D1.5 and D1.1.

Radiography licensing in Hawaii. Hawaii is not an NRC Agreement State. The US Nuclear Regulatory Commission, through its Region IV office, licenses and inspects the use of radioactive materials, including industrial radiography sources, in Hawaii under 10 CFR Part 34. Radiographers using sources must meet NRC radiographer certification and training requirements (the ASNT IRRSP examination is a common route). The State of Hawaii, through the Department of Health, has jurisdiction over X-ray equipment and certain other radiation sources. Atlantis RT method training covers technique and interpretation, not radiation safety licensing. Confirm current rules with the NRC and the Hawaii Department of Health before planning an RT programme.

Why corrosion shapes Hawaii training. In most mainland markets a new technician's first year is dominated by weld inspection on new construction. In Hawaii, much more of the work is in-service: finding and sizing wall loss, pitting and cracking on equipment that has been sitting in salt air for decades. That changes what a good training programme emphasises. UT thickness technique on corroded and coated surfaces, grid and scan planning, recognising the difference between a lamination and real wall loss, and recording data so that corrosion rates can be calculated later all matter more here than in a fabrication shop. Visual testing matters more too, because coating breakdown, corrosion under insulation indicators and pier and piling damage are often first spotted by eye. When Atlantis runs onsite practical sessions for a Hawaii crew, we build them around specimens that reflect that reality rather than generic clean weld coupons.

What local employers typically ask for. Hawaii job postings for NDT technicians commonly ask for SNT-TC-1A Level II in UT and at least one surface method, a clean driving record for field work across Oahu, and the ability to work at height or in confined spaces with the right safety training. Shipyard and military-installation roles add US citizenship and clearance requirements; refinery roles often add site safety orientations and API programme familiarity; aviation roles add OEM and airline-specific qualifications. SNT-TC-1A method certification is the common denominator.

For pay expectations, see the NDT salary guide.

Inter-island logistics for Hawaii NDT crews and equipment

Planning NDT training in Hawaii is as much a logistics exercise as a curriculum one. Most of the state's industrial inspection work is concentrated on Oahu, but power plants, harbours, fuel terminals, airports and bridges on Maui, the Big Island, Kauai and the other islands also need qualified technicians, and there is no road between islands. Every trip a technician makes to another island, or to the mainland, costs flights, accommodation and days away from the job.

That is why Atlantis structures Hawaii programmes around the smallest possible number of onsite visits. Classroom theory for every method and level on the programme runs live online first, so technicians on any island join from their own base. When the crew is ready for hands-on work, practical training, practical examinations, vision tests and any due recertifications are grouped into one onsite block at the employer's facility. Where an employer has technicians on more than one island, the usual approach is to bring the neighbour-island technicians to the main facility for that block, rather than repeating it on every island, though onsite sessions on a neighbour island can be arranged when the headcount justifies it.

Equipment is the second consideration. Shipping flaw detectors, probes, reference blocks, magnetic particle yokes and consumables to and from the mainland is slow, and some items, such as aerosol penetrants and developers, carry shipping restrictions by air. Training on the employer's own instruments and specimens avoids most of that, and it has a quality benefit too: technicians are examined on the same equipment and procedures they will use on the job. Before an onsite visit we agree with the employer which reference standards, calibration blocks and flawed specimens are on hand, and what consumables need to be ordered locally in advance.

Radiography needs extra planning. Because the NRC licenses radioactive materials in Hawaii, any source work during a practical session must be carried out under the employer's own licence and radiation safety programme, with its radiation safety officer involved. Many Hawaii employers therefore focus RT practical sessions on film and digital image interpretation, technique selection and image quality, which do not require exposing a source during training.

Finally, the calendar. Refinery and power plant outages, shipyard availability windows and military installation access all shape when crews can be released. Tell us your outage and project dates and we will fit theory around them and place the onsite block where it disrupts the least work. Plan a single onsite visit for your Hawaii crew.

Level III services and written practices for Hawaii NDT companies

Hawaii's NDT companies and in-house teams are often too small to justify a full-time Level III, yet the written practice, procedures and examinations still need Level III authority. Atlantis provides:

  • SNT-TC-1A written practice development and review. See written practice development.
  • Procedure writing for the methods and codes you use.
  • Examination administration and grading for general, specific and practical examinations, with practical examinations run onsite in Hawaii.
  • Audit preparation for owner and customer reviews.

Background: SNT-TC-1A training and certification. Book a Level III consultation for your Hawaii company.

Practise before the practical exam

The Practical NDT 3D simulator lets trainees practise 12 methods in 5 environments: an NDT lab, a welding workshop, an aircraft hangar, an oil and gas site and a storage tank. For Hawaii technicians, it is a useful way to rehearse between onsite visits. It is practice only and does not replace training hours, supervised experience or the practical examination on real specimens.

Your instructor

Training is led by Anoop Rayavarapu, ASNT NDT Level III and founder of Atlantis NDT, who develops course content, oversees practical sessions and examinations and supports employers with written practices and Level III services. See all NDT training programmes.

Frequently asked questions about NDT training in Hawaii

How do I get NDT certified in Hawaii?

Under SNT-TC-1A your employer certifies you after classroom training hours, documented experience, general, specific and practical examinations under a Level III, and a vision test. Atlantis provides training, practical preparation and, for employers, written practices and exams.

Can I take NDT training online in Hawaii?

Yes for classroom theory, with sessions arranged for Hawaii time. Practical training and the practical exam must be hands-on and run onsite at your employer's facility. See NDT training online.

How long does UT Level 2 training take?

It is set by the employer's written practice. SNT-TC-1A recommends minimum training and experience hours by level. See the training requirements matrix.

Do I need a license for radiography in Hawaii?

Hawaii is not an Agreement State, so the NRC licenses radioactive materials used in industrial radiography and radiographers must meet NRC certification requirements. X-ray equipment falls under the Hawaii Department of Health.

What does NDT training cost in Hawaii?

Quote on request. It depends on methods, levels, headcount, island and onsite requirements. Cohort and onsite quotes are normally returned within one business day. Request a Hawaii quote.

Is ASNT certification recognised by Hawaii employers?

Yes. SNT-TC-1A is the standard base for refinery, power, marine, aviation and inspection employers in Hawaii. Shipyard and aviation work add their own requirements on top.

Do I have to fly to the mainland for NDT training?

Not with Atlantis. Theory is online and practical training and examinations run onsite in Hawaii.

Does Atlantis offer API or NAVSEA certification?

No. Atlantis trains NDT methods under SNT-TC-1A only. API inspector and NAVSEA-specific qualifications are separate.

Do we need to ship NDT equipment to Hawaii for training?

Usually not. Practical training runs on your own instruments, reference blocks and specimens, which avoids shipping delays and restrictions on items such as aerosol penetrants. We agree the equipment and consumables list with you before the onsite visit.

Can you train crews on neighbour islands?

Yes, onsite at your facility on any island, subject to scheduling.

Can Atlantis act as our outside Level III?

Yes, including written practices, procedures and examinations. See written practice development.

Is there a simulator for practice?

Yes, Practical NDT. Practice only.

Where can I find practice questions?

See UT Level 2 practice questions.
